ContractHelp.NeedsHint: Pay below the Wealth equivalent draws on the stock or the treasury; above it is profit. 1 Wealth = 5 Supply ≈ 200 gold dragons.
ContractHelp.Rp1: Money scale: 1 Wealth ≈ 200 gold dragons (core book: 200 dragons donated to a house = +1 Wealth). Pay of 5 Wealth a month is about 1,000 dragons.
ContractHelp.Rp2: The employer has reasons and limits: urgency, enemies, an empty treasury, pride. Decide beforehand what they can concede and what would offend them.
ContractHelp.Rp3: Renown has a price: a famous company asks for more; an unknown one must prove itself (trial contract, smaller advance).
ContractHelp.Rp4: In the Free Cities, a contract is written, signed before witnesses and often backed by a bank: the Iron Bank of Braavos lends, advances and honors letters of credit.
ContractHelp.Rp5: A company's word is its capital: the Golden Company prides itself on never breaking a contract, while the Second Sons are known for changing sides.
ContractHelp.Rp6: Payment in kind is common: land, titles, prisoners to ransom, the right to sack a town. Handy when the employer lacks gold, risky for Cohesion if the men never see the coin.
ContractHelp.Title: Negotiate a contract: {name}
ContractHelp.Intro: Game aid: nothing is rolled or applied automatically. The Narrator runs the negotiation as they see fit, then fills in the Contract box.
ContractHelp.Step1: The Narrator sets the employer, duration and base pay from the mission, its danger and the Company's Renown.
ContractHelp.Step2: The Company's negotiator plays the scene; if it must be settled, a Persuasion (Bargain) test.
ContractHelp.Step3: Each degree of success may earn an improvement; a failure may add an unfavorable clause.
ContractHelp.Step4: The Narrator records the result in the Contract box (employer, pay, duration) and notes the clauses in the history.
ContractHelp.Lever1: Monthly pay, or a victory bonus.
ContractHelp.Lever4: Supplies provided by the employer, winter quarters.
ContractHelp.Lever5: Loot: right to plunder, share of ransoms, spoils of war.
ContractHelp.Bad1: Pay due at the end of the contract, or in kind.
ContractHelp.Bad2: No plundering, loot handed over to the employer.
ContractHelp.Bad3: Commander imposed by the employer, or a hostage as surety.
ContractHelp.NoServices: No staff or diplomacy service (Foreman, Aides-de-camp, Stewards, Negotiator, Spokesman).
ContractHelp.Reminder1: Breaking a contract or betraying an employer: −1d6 Renown.
ContractHelp.Reminder2: Loot and plunder pay on top of the contract; plundering costs −1 disposition with the region's people.
ContractHelp.Reminder3: Unpaid wages: −10% Cohesion per month; on the second month, desertions then risk of mutiny.
